docs/docs/api/Client.md:31:* **strictContentLength** `Boolean` (optional) - Default: `true` - Whether to treat request content length mismatches as errors. If true, an error is thrown when the request content-length header doesn't match the length of the request body. **Security Warning:** Disabling this option can expose your application to HTTP Request Smuggling attacks, where mismatched content-length headers cause servers and proxies to interpret request boundaries differently. This can lead to cache poisoning, credential hijacking, and bypassing security controls. Only disable this in controlled environments where you fully trust the request source.

content.text:
Fixed in `lib/core/request.js`.

## Change

`processHeader` parsed `content-length` with `parseInt(val, 10)`, which silently accepts anything with a numeric prefix: `"10.5"` → `10`, `"10abc"` → `10`, `" 10"` → `10`, `-1` stays `-1`, and a number like `1e21` (stringified to `"1e+21"`) → `1`. The normalized value then flowed into the body-length checks, surfacing later as a `RequestContentLengthMismatchError` — or not at all.

`lib/core/request.js:490` now requires a digit-only string before parsing:

```js
if (typeof val !== 'string' || !contentLengthRegex.test(val)) {
  throw new InvalidArgumentError('invalid content-length header')
}
request.contentLength = Number(val)
```

The existing `Number.isFinite` guard is kept — it is still reachable for digit strings long enough to overflow to `Infinity` (~309+ digits), which previously threw the same error.

Non-string values are normalized to strings earlier in the function, so numeric `10` still works (tests pass numbers); arrays and `null` are rejected, as `null` already was. Rejected now: `''`, `'10.5'`, `10.5`, `' 10'`, `'10abc'`, `'-1'`, `-1`, `'+1'`, `'1e3'`, `1e21`, `'abc'`, arrays. Accepted unchanged: `'0'`, `0`, `'10'`, `10`, `'007'` → `7`.

## Coupling checks (per COMPLEX.md)

- `lib/core/request.js` is a hotspot (34 fixes / 49 commits) but has no "Why these files are hot" paragraph, so no file-specific pre-edit ritual applied.
- Its read-first partner `lib/dispatcher/client.js` / `client-h1.js` / `client-h2.js`: I checked every `request.contentLength` consumer there. They compare an already-validated number against the body length and serialize it back out — no change needed.
- The `docs` ↔ `types` seam: no public API or type surface changed (`contentLength` is internal; the error class and code are unchanged), so no doc or `.d.ts` update needed.

## Tests

Added two cases to `test/content-length.js` — one asserting each malformed value yields `InvalidArgumentError('invalid content-length header')`, one asserting a valid value still reaches the wire as `content-length: 3`.

Passing: `test/content-length.js` (12), `test/no-strict-content-length.js` (7), plus `client-request`, `errors`, `headers-as-array`, `invalid-headers`, `prototype-headers`, `issue-2065`, `issue-803`, `trailers` (110), and `fetch/client-fetch`, `node-test/client-errors`, `client-pipeline` (95). I did not run `npm run lint` — the command required approval I didn't have. Nothing committed.
